newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to start Cambodia flight by end of March.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to start Cambodia flight by end of March.

text.p: Taiwan will begin commercial flights to Cambodia by the end of next month, despite protests from arch rival China, Taiwan's EVA Airways said on Thursday.
"We will launch our first flight by the end of March," Nieh Kuo-wei, spokesman for EVA Airways, a unit of shipping giant Evergreen Marine, said by telephone.

Taiwan's cabinet has given a final go-ahead to the Taiwan-Cambodia aviation agreement, signed quietly in December, to allow both countries to operate three commercial flights weekly, state media reported on Thursday.
Cambodia Airlines has yet to decide when to start its Taipei route, Nieh said.
The agreement was official despite the absence of diplomatic relations between Taiwan and Cambodia, which recognises only the communist Chinese government in Beijing.

Local media reports have said the pact was signed in secret to avoid pressure from China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province ineligible for international diplomatic ties since a civil war split them in 1949.
China has expressed anger at the aviation agreement, saying it was "firmly opposed" to its diplomatic allies establishing official air links with Taiwan.
"We don't expect any problems since the agreement is signed between Taiwan and Cambodia governments," Nieh said.
EVA, which plans to use either Boeing 767 or MD-90 wide-body jets for the service, said the route initially would be aimed at serving Taiwan businessmen investing in Cambodia.

Cambodia's co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen have stressed their commitment to a one-China policy while saying they welcome investment and businessmen from Taiwan, which maintains a trade office in Phnom Penh.
